risks.label: Purchased or forced views/subscribers
risks.limit: Third-party promoter can expose channel to removal; public engagement is not proof of authentic buyers

risks.label: False brand partnership and attachment
risks.limit: Verify through independent contact; suspicious documents and software may be malicious

risks.label: Account hijacking through links/downloads
risks.limit: Use passkeys/two-step verification and review access; no rate measured

risks.label: Deceptive off-platform purchase or support link
risks.limit: Scams and misleading destinations can violate platform rules and harm viewers

risks.label: Untrusted channel collaborator access
risks.limit: Delegate limited permissions without password sharing; periodically remove unknown managers

distinctions: A promotional budget spent under allowed rules is not the same as buying illegitimate view or subscriber engagement.
A claimed hacking threat is not verified compromise; avoid treating anecdotes as incident rates.
A legitimate sponsor inquiry does not require creator passwords or unsafe software downloads.
A phishing attempt, copyright claim, artificial engagement ban, and content-policy enforcement are different events.
Security settings may lower risk but these policy documents cannot estimate a numerical probability or cost reduction.
